mkdir -p /workspace/txt; for f in regulatory-undertaking remediation-plan ico-investigation-summary; do parse-doc docx documents/$f.docx > /workspace/txt/$f.txt; done; parse-doc xlsx documents/commitment-mapping-matrix.xlsx > /workspace/txt/matrix.txt; cp documents/plan-review-emails.eml /workspace/txt/emails.txt; wc -c /workspace/txt/*
cd /workspace/txt; split -b 40000 -d remediation-plan.txt rp_; ls -la rp_*; cat rp_00

python3 -c "import docx; print(docx.__version__ if hasattr(docx,\"__version__\") else \"ok\")"; ls /workspace/skills/docx/scripts/; grep -n "Gantt\|footnote\|technical notes" /workspace/txt/remediation-plan.txt | head

mkdir -p /workspace/build && cat > /workspace/build/rows.py <<"EOF"
# (no, title, phase, requirement, plan, gap, rating, recommendation)
ROWS = [
(1, "Automated Patch Management", "P1 – 14 Feb 2025",
 "Automated patching across all BellCloud UK components (OS, middleware, API gateways, DBMS, third-party libraries); critical/high (CVSS ≥7.0 or vendor rating, whichever higher) within 14 days of public disclosure; medium within 30 days; real-time dashboard viewable by DPO and IT security; monthly DPO review with sign-off and escalation to MD.",
 "Action 1 (PatchGuard Enterprise v8.2). Target 28 Feb 2025. 14-day cycle measured from “vendor patch availability”. Interim weekly manual patching overseen by Ridgeline. Owner: Dr Kassab / IT Infrastructure. £220,000.",
 "(1) Target date is 14 days after the Phase 1 deadline; Dr Kassab’s email (5 Feb) says “realistically into early March”. No extension request has been made under Cl. 7.6, and the 14-day request window closed on 31 Jan 2025. (2) Clock runs from “vendor patch availability”, not public disclosure as Commitment 1(a) requires. (3) No 30-day medium-severity SLA. (4) No CVSS-or-vendor “higher classification” rule. (5) No real-time dashboard for the DPO; no monthly DPO review, sign-off or escalation to the MD. (6) Scope is described only as “all BellCloud UK infrastructure”; DBMS, middleware and third-party libraries are not listed. (7) Interim manual patching does not meet the requirement for an automated system (Dr Kassab accepts this).",
 "Critical",
 "Notify the ICO now under Cl. 8.2 (material impediment, 5 business days) and make a late extension request under Cl. 7.6 that admits the missed window, gives full reasons, the interim controls and a firm revised date. Measure the SLA from public disclosure. Add the medium-severity SLA, the classification rule, the DPO dashboard and the monthly DPO sign-off and escalation. Escalate the PatchGuard MSA within BHS Inc. (Cl. 1.3: a delay at BHS Inc. is no defence). Keep dated logs of interim patching as evidence."),
(2, "Encryption Standards", "P1 – 14 Feb 2025",
 "AES-256 at rest for all personal data stores (databases, file stores, backups, archives); TLS 1.3 for all flows to, from and within BellCloud UK, with no fallback to TLS 1.2 or below and all lower-version cipher suites disabled on every endpoint; documented configurations; key management (generation, storage, rotation, destruction).",
 "Action 2. AES-256 at rest (databases, file stores, backup media). In transit: “TLS 1.2 or higher”, with a TLS 1.3 migration roadmap deferred to Phase 3. Target 14 Feb 2025. £310,000.",
 "(1) The Plan adopts a standard (TLS 1.2 fallback) that the Undertaking expressly prohibits. This is a unilateral variation, and under Cl. 11.1 a variation needs written agreement signed by both parties. (2) Emails confirm that 11 of 47 trusts are TLS 1.2-only, including 3 mental-health trusts holding roughly 12,000 of the 41,203 mental-health records, with an 18–24 month upgrade horizon. (3) TLS 1.0/1.1 use was a specific finding (Sch. 1 Finding 2). (4) Archive storage is not listed. (5) The Plan has no key-management procedure and no encryption configuration documentation (it lists TLS certificates only). (6) Cipher-suite disablement is not addressed.",
 "Critical",
 "Do not submit the Plan with “TLS 1.2 or higher” as if it complied. Enforce TLS 1.3-only on every endpoint BHS controls (internal service-to-service and the 36 compatible trusts) by 14 Feb. For the 11 legacy trusts, make a Cl. 11.2 variation request with reasons, impact and a proposed alternative of equivalent effect, for example TLS 1.3 to a BHS-managed edge proxy or IPsec/HSCN tunnel with TLS 1.2 limited to hardened AEAD cipher suites, a per-trust timetable and monthly reporting. Also notify under Cl. 8.2. Record trust engagement, as the DPO suggested. Add archives and key management."),
(3, "Access Controls", "P1 – 14 Feb 2025",
 "RBAC on least privilege mapped to job functions; automated provisioning; quarterly access reviews signed off by line manager and DPO; leaver and role-change revocation within 4 hours, enforced through HR-system integration.",
 "Action 3. RBAC, a one-off comprehensive access review, privilege revocation, role definitions, PAM. Target 12 Feb 2025. Owner: IT Security Lead. £185,000.",
 "(1) Automated provisioning is missing. (2) Only a one-off review is planned; recurring quarterly reviews with line-manager and DPO sign-off are missing. (3) The 4-hour leaver/role-change revocation and HR integration are missing. This matters because the ICO found 8 of 23 unrestricted admin accounts belonged to leavers. The matrix wrongly records Commitment 3 as fully aligned.",
 "High",
 "Add an HR-integrated joiner-mover-leaver workflow with a 4-hour revocation SLA and logging; a quarterly review calendar (first review by end Q2 2025) with documented line-manager and DPO sign-off; and automated provisioning. Add evidence lines: HR-integration test results and revocation timestamp reports."),
(4, "Network Segmentation", "P2 – 15 Apr 2025",
 "Isolate (a) patient data zones from corporate IT (no direct path); (b) production from all Non-Production Environments, with controlled and logged flows; (c) each NHS trust’s data from other trusts, logically, at application and infrastructure level; (d) admin pathways from data pathways, using dedicated hardened management interfaces.",
 "Action 4. Patient data isolated from corporate networks, development environments and public-facing services; micro-segmentation, ACLs, firewall rules. Target 10 Apr 2025. £275,000.",
 "(1) Production is segregated only from “development environments”, not all Non-Production Environments as defined in Cl. 3.1 (staging, QA, UAT, analytics, reporting, data warehouse, sandboxes). (2) No control or logging of production-to-non-production flows. (3) Per-trust logical separation is missing. (4) Separation of the administrative pathway and hardened management interfaces is missing.",
 "High",
 "Extend scope to all Non-Production Environments and to logged, approved data flows; add per-trust tenancy separation with test evidence; add a dedicated admin plane and jump hosts; and test segmentation independently (could form part of the first independent penetration test)."),
(5, "API Security", "P2 – 15 Apr 2025",
 "API gateway with rate limiting, authentication, input validation and schema enforcement for all external APIs; API security testing at least quarterly (automated and manual); complete API inventory (purpose, authentication, data exposure, risk class); legacy endpoints deprecated within 30 days of identification.",
 "Action 5. WAF, rate limiting, input validation, authN/authZ, schema enforcement; evidence includes API inventory and risk classification. Target 8 Apr 2025. £195,000.",
 "(1) No quarterly API security testing cadence. (2) No 30-day legacy endpoint deprecation rule. (3) The inventory fields required by Commitment 5(c) are not specified.",
 "Medium",
 "Add a quarterly API test schedule (automated and manual), a 30-day deprecation SLA with a tracking log, and the required inventory fields."),
(6, "Penetration Testing", "P2 – 15 Apr 2025",
 "Independent CREST-accredited external testing each quarter (at least 4 per calendar year). The provider must not have provided forensic, remediation or other Breach-related services; Ridgeline is expressly excluded. Critical/high findings fixed within 30 days of the report; full reports available to the ICO on request.",
 "Action 7. Bi-annual tests (2 a year) by Ridgeline, chosen for its “extensive knowledge of the BellCloud UK architecture”. First test 15 Apr 2025. £160,000 (two tests).",
 "(1) Ridgeline is expressly excluded by name. Appointing it breaches Commitment 6 outright, and its forensic and remediation role is the reason for the exclusion. (2) Frequency is half the requirement. (3) There is no 30-day remediation SLA. (4) There is no provision to make reports available to the ICO. (5) The budget covers only 2 tests. (6) With a first test in April, 4 tests in calendar 2025 needs a compressed schedule.",
 "Critical",
 "Remove Ridgeline. Procure an unconnected CREST provider now so the first test is done by 15 Apr 2025, and confirm independence in writing (no Breach-related services). Schedule quarterly tests (for example Apr, Jun, Sep, Dec 2025) to reach 4 in 2025, or get ICO confirmation of the 2025 count. Add the 30-day critical/high SLA and ICO access, and re-budget for 4 tests a year."),
(7, "Vulnerability Scanning", "P2 – 15 Apr 2025",
 "Continuous automated scanning of all internet-facing and internal systems; at least weekly; results triaged by qualified personnel within 48 hours; remediation workflow integrated with the Commitment 1 patch system.",
 "Action 6. Continuous scanning, weekly cycles, risk-prioritised workflows, PatchGuard integration; covers production, staging and development. Target 5 Apr 2025. Owner: Ridgeline. £130,000.",
 "(1) No 48-hour triage SLA or qualified-personnel requirement. (2) Scope omits QA, UAT, analytics, reporting and other non-production systems. (3) Integration depends on PatchGuard, which is itself late (C1).",
 "Medium",
 "Add the 48-hour triage SLA with named qualified triage staff, extend scope to all in-scope systems, and define a stop-gap ticketing integration until PatchGuard is live."),
(8, "Logging and Monitoring (SIEM)", "P2 – 15 Apr 2025",
 "Centralised SIEM capturing access, authentication (including failed attempts), data exports, admin actions, configuration changes and privilege escalations; 12-month retention in a tamper-evident, immutable store; real-time alerts for anomalies (unusual access, high-volume exports, unusual locations, repeated failed logins); 24/7 monitoring by qualified staff or a managed SOC.",
 "Action 8. SIEM with real-time alerting for “all access to personal data stores”; 12-month tamper-evident retention. Target 12 Apr 2025. £210,000.",
 "(1) Event coverage is limited to data-store access; the other event classes are missing. (2) The store is described as tamper-evident but not immutable. (3) The required alert use-cases are not specified. (4) There is no 24/7 monitoring commitment (in-house or managed SOC). (5) There is no automated SIEM alert to the DPO, which C33 requires.",
 "High",
 "Specify all Commitment 8(a) event classes, an immutable (WORM) store, the 8(c) use-cases, and a contracted 24/7 SOC with SLAs. Link SIEM alerts to automatic DPO notification under C33."),
(9, "Multi-Factor Authentication", "P2 – 15 Apr 2025",
 "MFA for all admin access, all remote staff access (VPN, RDP etc.), all access to special category data (local or remote), and all third-party access including NHS trust and clinic users through portals or APIs. At least two factors from different categories; SMS OTP not acceptable as a sole second factor.",
 "Action 9. MFA for administrative and user access, PAM, developers, clinical data portals; hardware tokens and authenticator apps. Evidence includes an “exception register”. Target 14 Apr 2025. £165,000.",
 "(1) Remote-access channels and third-party/partner API access are not expressly covered. (2) No prohibition on SMS as a sole factor. (3) No different-category factor rule. (4) The “exception register” implies exceptions the Undertaking does not allow.",
 "High",
 "Expressly cover VPN/RDP and all partner portal and API access (machine-to-machine: mutual TLS or OAuth with strong client authentication), ban SMS as a sole factor, and replace the exception register with a nil-exceptions attestation (or an ICO-agreed variation)."),
(10, "DPIA Framework", "P2 – 15 Apr 2025",
 "Criteria for when a DPIA is required (Art. 35 and ICO guidance); standard methodology and templates; DPO sign-off on all DPIAs before processing begins; DPIA screening built into project and change control so nothing proceeds without screening.",
 "Action 10 (framework, methodology, criteria, change-management integration; approved by the Steering Committee); Action 16 (template library); Action 15 (PM training, 14 Jul). Target 15 Apr 2025.",
 "(1) There is no requirement for DPO sign-off before processing. The Plan names Steering Committee approval instead, a body that includes BHS Inc.’s General Counsel and Ridgeline. (2) There is no “no screening, no go” gate in change control.",
 "Medium",
 "Make DPO sign-off a mandatory pre-processing gate and add a mandatory screening step to change control, with evidence of the change-control configuration."),
(11, "Retrospective DPIAs", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Retrospective DPIAs on all existing processing involving personal data in BellCloud UK, prioritising special category data, completed within 180 days; each assessing necessity and proportionality, risks and mitigations.",
 "Action 11. Retrospective DPIAs on all existing high-risk processing after a screening exercise. Target 10 Jul 2025. £90,000.",
 "The scope is narrowed from all processing in BellCloud UK to high-risk processing only. Sch. 1 Finding 6 records that no BellCloud UK DPIA existed. The Plan does not state the required content (necessity, proportionality, risks, mitigations).",
 "High",
 "Restore the full scope (every BellCloud UK processing activity, prioritising special category data), state the required DPIA content, and set an interim milestone (for example 15 May 2025) for the special category DPIAs."),
(12, "DPIA Review Triggers", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Documented triggers: (a) any new processing; (b) significant changes to purpose, scope, context or technology; (c) changes to the risk environment (threat intelligence, regulation, new vulnerabilities); (d) at least an annual review of all DPIAs.",
 "Action 12. Triggers for changes to processing, new data types, new technologies, significant system changes; integrated with project and change management. Target 14 Jul 2025.",
 "Triggers for changes to the risk environment (c) and the mandatory annual review (d) are missing. New processing (a) is only implicit.",
 "Medium",
 "Add triggers (a), (c) and (d) and an annual review calendar linked to the DPIA register."),
(13, "ICO Consultation Threshold", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Formal documented Art. 36 process where residual risk stays high after mitigation; every decision on whether to consult documented, with reasons for not consulting and DPO sign-off.",
 "Action 13. Internal threshold and escalation process for high residual risk. Target 14 Jul 2025.",
 "No requirement to document every consultation decision and the reasons for not consulting, and no DPO sign-off on those decisions.",
 "Medium",
 "Add a decision log with reasons and DPO sign-off for every high-risk DPIA outcome."),
(14, "DPIA Register", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Central register accessible to the DPO and to the ICO on request; lists DPIAs, review dates, outcomes, residual risks accepted by senior management with justification, and next review date; updated within 5 business days of any DPIA completion or review.",
 "Action 14. Register accessible to the DPO and senior management, recording DPIAs, review dates, outcomes, residual risk; DPIA tool. Target 14 Jul 2025. £55,000.",
 "(1) No ICO access on request. (2) No record of senior-management risk acceptance with justification. (3) No next-review-date field. (4) No 5-business-day update SLA.",
 "Medium",
 "Add the missing fields, ICO access, and the 5-business-day update SLA."),
(15, "Processor Audit Programme", "P2 – 15 Apr 2025",
 "At least annual audit of every processor covering DPA compliance, TOMs, sub-processor management and data subject rights fulfilment; DPO review of every report; material non-compliance escalated to the MD and, where appropriate, the board.",
 "Action 17. Risk-based programme with annual audits of all processors; inventory; risk classification; enhanced frequency for high-risk processors; remediation process. Target 15 Apr 2025. £120,000.",
 "(1) Audit content areas are not specified. (2) No DPO review of each report. (3) No escalation route to the MD or board. (4) The programme does not reach sub-processors (see C17).",
 "Medium",
 "Specify the four audit areas, DPO review, and the MD/board escalation route. Prioritise the 7 of 12 processor relationships the ICO found deficient."),
(16, "Updated Article 28 Agreements", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "All DPAs updated and executed to include every Art. 28(3) term: (a) documented instructions; (b) confidentiality; (c) security; (d) sub-processor conditions; (e) data subject rights assistance; (f) breach and DPIA assistance; (g) deletion or return; (h) audit rights.",
 "Action 18. Clauses on subject matter, duration, nature and purpose, data types, controller obligations, sub-processing, audit rights, return and deletion, international transfers. Target 10 Jul 2025. £95,000.",
 "Terms (a) documented instructions, (b) confidentiality, (c) Art. 32 security, (e) data subject rights assistance and (f) breach and DPIA assistance are not listed. Execution depends on processor cooperation (Plan §14 risk 3) with no fallback.",
 "Medium",
 "Map the DPA template clause by clause to Art. 28(3)(a)–(h), add a fallback (suspend or replace non-signing processors), and track execution per processor."),
(17, "Sub-Processor Due Diligence", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Pre-engagement privacy risk assessment of every sub-processor; annual sub-processor compliance audits; Art. 28 flow-down through the chain; register of approved sub-processors (identity, location, scope) available to the ICO; no sub-processor engaged without BHS UK’s prior written authorisation.",
 "No action item, no owner, no budget. Missing from Appendix A, the WS3 table and the matrix. The only related text is Action 18 (“sub-processing restrictions and approval mechanisms”) and Action 21 (an international-only sub-processor transfer register).",
 "The commitment is not addressed at all. The ICO called the absence of sub-processor due diligence a “discrete and significant failing” (ICO letter, Finding 7), and Sch. 1 Finding 8 notes BHS UK could not produce a list of sub-processors. The Plan’s claim to address all 47 commitments is wrong.",
 "Critical",
 "Create a new action item (owner: DPO and Procurement; target on or before 14 Jul 2025, with an interim register by 15 May 2025) covering a full sub-processor census, pre-engagement assessments, an annual audit schedule, flow-down clauses, an ICO-accessible register, and a prior-written-authorisation control. Fund it and correct Appendix A, the WS3 narrative and the matrix."),
(18, "Processor Breach Notification Chain", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Processors and sub-processors contractually bound to notify BHS UK without undue delay and within 24 hours of discovery; documented chain to the DPO with immediate triage; minimum content (nature, categories and approximate numbers of data subjects, containment and remediation measures).",
 "Action 19. “Without undue delay and within contractually defined timeframes”; content, contacts, channels and escalation; built into the Action 18 DPAs. Target 14 Jul 2025.",
 "(1) No 24-hour maximum. (2) Sub-processors are not expressly bound. (3) Routing to the DPO with immediate triage is not stated. (4) The minimum content items are not enumerated.",
 "High",
 "Hard-code the 24-hour maximum for processors and sub-processors, direct notices to the DPO, and list the minimum content items."),
(19, "Processor Data Return/Deletion", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Contractual return or secure deletion on termination with written certification; checked through the C15 audit programme; certificates kept for the term of the Undertaking plus 2 years.",
 "Action 20. Contractual certified deletion, verification (certificates, independent verification), evidence kept for audit. Target 14 Jul 2025. £60,000.",
 "Retention of certificates for the term plus 2 years and the link to C15 verification are not stated.",
 "Low",
 "Add the retention period (consistent with Cl. 10.2) and the C15 verification step."),
(20, "International Transfer Safeguards", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Appropriate safeguards (s.119A SCCs/IDTA/Addendum and TRAs) for all restricted transfers, including to processors, sub-processors and group entities, expressly including BHS Inc. (US); a register of all international transfers with safeguards documented.",
 "Action 21. Limited to “third-party sub-processors” in non-adequate jurisdictions: IDTAs or Addenda, TRAs, a sub-processor transfer register. Target 14 Jul 2025. £160,000.",
 "The Plan omits the very transfer the ICO found unlawful: routine intra-group transfers of health data to BHS Inc. in Austin with no safeguard and no TRA (Sch. 1 Finding 12; ICO Finding 8). Direct processors are also omitted, and the register covers sub-processors only. The UK Extension to the EU-US DPF is not assessed, although the ICO said it must be specifically assessed and documented.",
 "Critical",
 "Expand scope to all restricted transfers, with BHS Inc. first. Execute an IDTA or Addendum with BHS Inc. (or document reliance on the UK Extension if BHS Inc. is certified and the data categories are covered), complete a TRA, and minimise or suspend transfers that are not needed. Bring the BHS Inc. transfer forward to before 15 Apr 2025, given its ongoing unlawfulness. Keep a register of all transfers. Feed the results into the C44 privacy notices."),
(21, "Mandatory Annual Training", "P2 – 15 Apr 2025",
 "Annual training for all UK staff (342 plus new hires), delivered by a qualified external provider approved by the DPO, with assessed competency; curriculum (a)–(f) including the C33 escalation SLA, role-relevant duties and Undertaking obligations; new joiners within 30 days; records kept for the term.",
 "Action 24. Internally developed e-learning on the BHS LMS; 80% pass mark; curriculum covers GDPR principles, breach reporting, special category data, rights, minimisation and retention, scenarios. 100% completion within 30 days of module launch. Target 15 Apr 2025. £45,000.",
 "(1) Internal delivery contradicts the express external-provider requirement. The ICO also criticised the lack of “qualified and externally delivered training”. (2) No DPO approval of the provider. (3) Curriculum items (c) (the C33 SLA), (e) role-relevant obligations and (f) Undertaking obligations are missing. (4) No 30-day new-joiner rule. (5) If the module launches on 15 Apr, completion may not happen until mid-May, after the Phase 2 deadline. (6) There is no budget for an external provider.",
 "High",
 "Engage a qualified external provider (DPO-approved), budget for it, add the missing curriculum items and the new-joiner rule, and set the launch date so that 100% completion falls on or before 15 Apr 2025."),
(22, "Role-Based Specialist Training", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Specialist training at least annually for high-risk roles, including IT security, development, clinical data management, customer support and data analytics; DPO approval of content and scope.",
 "Action 25. External providers for IT security, developers, clinical data managers, privacy team and customer-facing DSR staff. Target 14 Jul 2025. £120,000.",
 "(1) Data analytics staff are missing, although the analytics and reporting environments hold un-pseudonymised special category data. (2) No annual cadence. (3) No DPO approval.",
 "Medium",
 "Add analytics and reporting staff, the annual cadence, and DPO approval of content."),
(23, "Phishing Simulation", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "At least quarterly simulations for all staff; results tracked at individual and team level; targeted remedial training for failures; aggregate results to the DPO and in the quarterly board reports.",
 "Action 26. Monthly simulations; follow-up training within 7 days; quarterly results to the Steering Committee and board reporting. Target 14 Jul 2025. £60,000.",
 "Frequency exceeds the requirement. Individual and team-level tracking and reporting to the DPO are not stated.",
 "Low",
 "Add individual and team tracking and express reporting to the DPO."),
(24, "Training Completion KPIs", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "100% completion within 30 days of each annual cycle; 95% pass rate on competency assessments with extra training for those below; disciplinary escalation for non-completion.",
 "Action 27. Training management system, KPI dashboard; 100% completion KPI stated in Action 24. Target 14 Jul 2025. £45,000.",
 "(1) No 95% pass-rate KPI. (2) No disciplinary escalation. The matrix also misstates this commitment as “95% completion”.",
 "Medium",
 "Add the 95% pass-rate KPI, the remedial-training loop, and disciplinary escalation under HR policy."),
(25, "Board-Level Reporting on Training", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Training metrics (completion, scores, phishing results, remedial actions) in quarterly board reports; the DPO presents training metrics as a standing item at every board meeting.",
 "Action 22 (cross-funded in WS7). Quarterly board reporting on completion, competency and awareness metrics. Target 15 Apr 2025. £12,000.",
 "(1) No standing DPO agenda item at every board meeting. (2) Remedial actions are not covered. (3) The board is not identified as the BHS UK board (see C38). The early target date is acceptable.",
 "Medium",
 "Make DPO training metrics a standing item at every BHS UK Ltd board meeting and add remedial-action reporting."),
(26, "DPO Resource Allocation", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Dedicated privacy team of at least 4 FTE; no reduction without prior ICO written approval; the DPO’s budget reported to the board quarterly.",
 "Action 23 (WS7). +2 FTE plus training coordination resource. Target 14 Jul 2025. £18,000 (recruitment only; salaries funded outside the budget).",
 "(1) The Plan does not state the current headcount, so it cannot show that the team will reach at least 4 FTE. (2) No non-reduction safeguard. (3) No quarterly reporting of the DPO budget. (4) The salary source is unconfirmed. The matrix misdescribes the commitment as “minimum 2 additional FTEs”.",
 "High",
 "State the baseline and confirm at least 4 dedicated FTE by 14 Jul 2025 (recruit more if the baseline is under 2). Record a board resolution on salary funding and the non-reduction undertaking. Add quarterly DPO budget reporting."),
(27, "Retention Schedule Overhaul", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Lawful retention periods for all personal data categories with documented justification (legal basis and purpose); DPO approval; at least annual review.",
 "Action 28 (plus Action 33 classification). Periods, legal bases, deletion triggers, NHS Records Management Code alignment; approval records. Target 10 Jul 2025. £75,000.",
 "DPO approval and the annual review are not expressly stated. The schedule lands on 10 Jul, which leaves C28 and C31 (due 14 Jul) almost no time to run against it.",
 "Low",
 "Name the DPO as approver, add an annual review, and bring the target forward (for example to 30 May 2025) so C28 and C31 can run against it."),
(28, "Automated Deletion Workflows", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Automated secure deletion on retention expiry; each deletion logged (category, expired retention period, date, method); monthly deletion reports to the DPO.",
 "Action 29. Automated workflows to “securely delete or anonymise”, with audit-trail logging. Target 14 Jul 2025. £85,000.",
 "(1) The deletion-log fields are not specified. (2) No monthly DPO reports. (3) “Anonymise” is an alternative the Undertaking does not provide; it is acceptable only if the data is truly anonymous. (4) The timing depends on C27.",
 "Medium",
 "Specify the log fields and monthly DPO reports, and limit anonymisation to documented, tested irreversible anonymisation, or remove it."),
(29, "Pseudonymisation Roadmap", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Defined technical standards (separating identifiers, protecting the re-identification key); milestones at 60, 120 and 180 days (16 Mar, 15 May, 14 Jul 2025); 100% of special category health data pseudonymised in all Non-Production Environments (test, dev, staging, QA, analytics, reporting) by 14 Jul 2025; no un-pseudonymised special category data in any Non-Production Environment after that date.",
 "Action 32. Scope: “test and development environments” only; 85% coverage target; the remaining coverage left to a “subsequent phase”; tokenisation and “irreversible hashing”; central token service with key separation. Target 14 Jul 2025. £95,000.",
 "(1) Coverage is 85%, not 100%. (2) Staging, QA, analytics and reporting are excluded, although Cl. 3.1 and Commitment 29 itself define them as in scope. The DPO’s email (6 Feb) is wrong to say the term is undefined. (3) There are no 60/120/180-day milestones. (4) Deferring to a “subsequent phase” amounts to an unapproved extension. (5) Dr Kassab puts the cost of full compliance at £280,000–£340,000 more, which is not budgeted. (6) “Irreversible hashing” is inconsistent with a re-identification key model, and unsalted hashes of NHS numbers can be reversed by enumeration. (7) The ICO identified 41,203 mental-health records in non-production environments (ICO Finding 10).",
 "Critical",
 "Restate the target as 100% across all Non-Production Environments by 14 Jul 2025, with the 60/120/180-day milestones. If full masking cannot be built in time, reach compliance by removing un-pseudonymised special category data from staging, QA, analytics and reporting (synthetic or masked datasets, or shutting down feeds) rather than accepting a residual 15%. Fund the gap (Recital 2.9 confirms BHS UK has the resources). Specify keyed tokenisation or HMAC with key separation. If any risk to the 14 Jul date remains, notify under Cl. 8.2 and request an extension by 30 Jun 2025."),
(30, "Data Minimisation Review", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Comprehensive review of all processing (BellCloud UK and wider operations) to identify and eliminate processing that is not strictly necessary, with focus on special category data; carried out by the DPO’s team; formal report with findings presented to the board.",
 "Action 30. Systematic review of adequacy, relevance and necessity; report and tracker. Target 14 Jul 2025. £50,000.",
 "(1) No obligation to eliminate unnecessary processing. (2) No board presentation. (3) No special category focus. (4) The DPO’s team is not named as the reviewer.",
 "Medium",
 "Add the elimination obligation, special category priority, DPO-team ownership, and board presentation."),
(31, "Storage Limitation Audit", "P3 – 14 Jul 2025",
 "Audit to find data held beyond retention; secure deletion within 60 days of identification; results reported to the DPO and board.",
 "Action 31 (plus Action 34 legacy clean-up). Audit of all stores; identifies over-retained data and “initiates remediation”. Target 14 Jul 2025. £45,000.",
